title: A Forest Beneath the Water
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。一般的原理と架空の例を用いた文章。架空例は実在の調査・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A forest does not always consist of trees growing on dry ground.
sentences.ja: 森は必ずしも乾いた地面に生える木々から成るわけではない。

sentences.en: Along some tropical coasts, mangrove trees grow in places where land and sea meet.
sentences.ja: 熱帯の一部の海岸では、陸と海が出会う場所にマングローブの木が生える。

sentences.en: Their roots and surrounding sediment create a complex environment in which many small organisms can find food or shelter.
sentences.ja: 根と周囲の堆積物は、多くの小さな生物が食物やすみかを見つけられる複雑な環境を作る。

sentences.en: At high tide, parts of this landscape may be hidden beneath the water, making its ecological importance less obvious to a visitor.
sentences.ja: 満潮時には景観の一部が水面下に隠れ、生態学的重要性が訪問者に分かりにくくなることがある。

sentences.en: The conditions in such an environment present challenges that differ from those faced by trees in an ordinary inland forest.
sentences.ja: その環境の条件は、一般的な内陸の森の木々が直面するものとは異なる課題をもたらす。

sentences.en: The amount of salt in the surrounding water can vary, and the wet ground may contain relatively little oxygen available to roots.
sentences.ja: 周囲の水の塩分量は変化し、湿った地面には根が利用できる酸素が比較的少ない場合がある。

sentences.en: Different mangrove species possess different adaptations that allow them to survive under some combination of these conditions.
sentences.ja: 異なるマングローブ種は、それらの条件の組み合わせのもとで生き残るための異なる適応形質を持つ。

sentences.en: However, adaptations do not make plants completely independent of their environment or able to tolerate every possible change.
sentences.ja: しかし適応形質があっても植物が環境から完全に独立したり、あらゆる変化に耐えたりできるわけではない。

sentences.en: Imagine a coastal community considering how to use an area of land near a mangrove forest.
sentences.ja: マングローブ林近くの土地の利用法を検討する沿岸地域を想像しよう。

sentences.en: A map showing only the places where people can build might present the forest as an obstacle to further development.
sentences.ja: 建設可能な場所だけを示す地図は、森を開発の障害として示すかもしれない。

sentences.en: A different map could indicate channels through which water moves and areas where young fish might seek protection.
sentences.ja: 別の地図は水の流れる水路や小魚が保護を求める場所を示せるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The second map would encourage people to examine connections that the first map was not designed to represent.
sentences.ja: 第二の地図は第一の地図が表すよう設計されていないつながりを調べるよう促すだろう。

sentences.en: Such a comparison would not establish the appropriate management plan for an actual coastline.
sentences.ja: この比較は実際の海岸の適切な管理計画を確立するものではない。

sentences.en: Decisions would require local observations, ecological assessments, and consideration of the activities and needs of nearby communities.
sentences.ja: 判断には現地観察、生態学的評価、近隣地域の活動と必要への考慮が必要になる。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the example illustrates why an area that appears unproductive according to one measure may perform functions that are valuable in another context.
sentences.ja: それでも一尺度で非生産的に見える場所が、別の文脈で価値ある機能を果たす理由を例示する。

sentences.en: The usefulness of a map depends partly on the questions that guided its creation.
sentences.ja: 地図の有用性は作成を導いた問いにも依存する。

sentences.en: A channel that is too small to appear prominently on a map may nevertheless connect habitats used by different species.
sentences.ja: 地図で目立たないほど小さい水路も、異なる種が利用する生息環境を結びつけている場合がある。

sentences.en: A mangrove forest invites us to consider the relationship between visible natural features and the less visible processes occurring around them.
sentences.ja: マングローブ林は目に見える自然特徴と周囲で起きる見えにくい過程の関係を考えるよう促す。

sentences.en: Environmental value cannot always be understood by examining isolated objects on a map.
sentences.ja: 環境の価値は地図の個別対象を調べるだけでは常に理解できない。

sentences.en: It may instead become apparent through the relationships between organisms, water, soil, and human activities.
sentences.ja: むしろ生物、水、土、人間活動の関係から明らかになる場合がある。

sentences.en: The spaces between the trees are part of the forest, too.
sentences.ja: 木々の間の空間も森の一部なのだ。

vocabulary.definition: relating to hot regions near the equator
regular rise or fall of sea level
relating to organisms and their environment
process of developing land or activities

options: In coastal places where land and sea meet.

questions.prompt: Why may visitors overlook part of the forest?
options: All trees disappear permanently at high tide.
High tide can hide parts of it.
The forest has no organisms below water.
questions.explanation_ja: 満潮時に水面下に隠れる。

options: Variable salt levels and limited oxygen in wet ground.
A lack of all available water.

questions.prompt: Why does the author qualify the value of adaptations?
options: They remove the need for roots.
They help under certain conditions but do not guarantee survival under every change.

questions.prompt: What might the second map indicate?
options: Water channels and places where young fish seek shelter.
A development map has no legitimate purpose.
They reveal different aspects of the same area.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的によって見える要素が異なる。

questions.prompt: What is needed for actual decisions?
options: A universal rule prohibiting all activity.
Local observations, assessments and consideration of community needs.
questions.explanation_ja: 現地の情報と地域の必要。

questions.prompt: What can an apparently unproductive area do?
options: Perform valuable functions overlooked by a particular measure.
Provide no useful function by definition.
questions.explanation_ja: 測定尺度で見えない価値。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the passage?
options: Mangrove forests should all have identical management plans.
A map of building sites explains every environmental function.
Environmental value becomes clearer by examining relationships and processes, not just individual features.
Only visible trees contribute to coastal environments.
questions.explanation_ja: 環境の価値は関係と過程から理解する。

grammar.explanation_ja: thoseはchallengesの代用、過去分詞修飾。
